summary: Nintendo's high-speed futuristic racing series, covering the SNES original, Satellaview broadcasts, N64/64DD releases, GBA games, GameCube/arcade GX-AX pair, and the Switch Online battle royale revival.

entries.title: F-Zero
entries.definitive_edition: Original SNES version via Nintendo Switch Online

emulation.notes: SNES emulation is the fallback if not using Nintendo Switch Online.

primary.version: Original SNES release via current official emulation
primary.why: The original F-Zero is available through Nintendo Switch Online's SNES library, making it the best current official route for the launch game.
primary.how_to_play: Play F-Zero through Nintendo Switch Online SNES, or use a legally dumped SNES cartridge in bsnes/Mesen.

all_releases.reason: skip: authentic original, but current official emulation is easier to access.

all_releases.platform: SNES Classic Edition / Virtual Console / Nintendo Switch Online
all_releases.reason: primary: current official route is Nintendo Switch Online.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Official emulated releases preserve the original game.

entries.remaster_caveats: F-Zero 99 is a battle-royale reinterpretation and is cataloged separately.

entries.title: BS F-Zero Grand Prix

primary.why: BS F-Zero Grand Prix was a Satellaview broadcast release with no modern official port, so the preserved broadcast version is the only route.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved Satellaview broadcast data with a compatible SNES/Satellaview emulator where legally available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability depends on preservation of broadcast data.

entries.title: BS F-Zero Grand Prix 2

primary.why: BS F-Zero Grand Prix 2 was a second Satellaview broadcast release and has no documented modern official port.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved Satellaview broadcast data with a compatible SNES/Satellaview emulator where legally available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability depends on preservation of broadcast data.

entries.title: F-Zero X

emulation.notes: Use hardware or emulation that supports the 64DD expansion disk.

primary.why: The Japan-only 64DD Expansion Kit adds 12 tracks across two cups plus machine and course editors, making it the most complete F-Zero X route; Nintendo Switch Online preserves the standard N64 game but not the Expansion Kit.
primary.how_to_play: Use original N64/64DD hardware or a preservation setup that supports the F-Zero X Expansion Kit; use Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack for the standard F-Zero X release.

secondary.exclusive_content: Current official standard F-Zero X release with online multiplayer support.
secondary.what_to_play: Use for convenient standard F-Zero X access.
secondary.why: It lacks the 64DD Expansion Kit content but is the official current route.

all_releases.reason: skip: base game is less complete than Expansion Kit route.

all_releases.fidelity: Expansion disk with added cups, tracks, machine creator, course editor, and music.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete F-Zero X content route.

all_releases.platform: iQue Player / Virtual Console / Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack
all_releases.fidelity: Official re-releases of the standard game; NSO adds online multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: secondary: current official standard-game route but lacks Expansion Kit content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Expansion Kit is most complete but rare/Japan-only; Nintendo Switch Online is the current official accessible standard version.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official release includes the Expansion Kit content.

entries.title: F-Zero X Expansion Kit

emulation.notes: Needs 64DD support and legally preserved disk data.

primary.why: The Expansion Kit is a Japan-only 64DD add-on requiring the F-Zero X cartridge, adding two cups, 12 tracks, a course editor, a machine creator, and extra music.
primary.how_to_play: Play with F-Zero X on original N64/64DD hardware or a preservation emulator/setup that supports the disk.

all_releases.fidelity: Original disk expansion for F-Zero X.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official release of the expansion content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires the base F-Zero X cartridge; no current official rerelease.

entries.definitive_edition: Original GBA version via Nintendo Switch Online

entries.title: F-Zero GX
entries.definitive_edition: F-Zero GX with AX content unlocked

emulation.notes: Dolphin can raise GameCube internal resolution; AX preservation is separate and more specialized.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: GameCube emulation at high internal resolution / Switch 2 official release

primary.version: F-Zero GX with AX content unlocked
primary.why: GX is the core home version and can unlock AX tracks/vehicles; it was also rereleased through Nintendo Classics on Switch 2 in 2025, giving it a current official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play F-Zero GX through Nintendo Classics on Switch 2 where available, or use the GameCube release on Dolphin with legally dumped media and unlock AX content through in-game challenges.

secondary.exclusive_content: Arcade cabinet experience, AX tracks/vehicles, and memory-card connectivity with GX.
secondary.what_to_play: Play AX if you can access a cabinet or preserved Triforce setup.
secondary.why: AX has a distinct arcade format even though much of its content can connect back to GX.

all_releases.reason: skip: original route, but current Switch 2 official release or Dolphin can improve access/fidelity.

all_releases.fidelity: Current official rerelease of the GameCube title.
all_releases.reason: primary: official modern route for GX.

all_releases.fidelity: Triforce arcade counterpart with cabinet-specific experience.
all_releases.reason: secondary: distinct arcade content/format tied to GX connectivity.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Switch 2/Nintendo Classics is the current official route; Dolphin can exceed it for raw internal resolution, and AX remains a distinct arcade experience.

entries.remaster_caveats: AX should be sampled separately if arcade cabinet format matters.

entries.title: F-Zero AX

emulation.notes: AX preservation is more specialized than normal GameCube Dolphin usage.

primary.why: F-Zero AX is the arcade counterpart to F-Zero GX, using Triforce hardware and offering cabinet-specific play, memory-card connectivity, AX tracks, and AX vehicles.
primary.how_to_play: Play on an original F-Zero AX cabinet where available, or use a preserved Triforce-compatible setup.

secondary.exclusive_content: GX can unlock AX tracks, pilots, vehicles, and parts through difficult challenges or arcade connectivity.
secondary.what_to_play: Unlock the AX content in GX for home access.
secondary.why: It captures much of AX's content without the physical arcade cabinet.

all_releases.reason: primary: only official release of the AX arcade game.
secondary: content access without cabinet format.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: AX is an arcade-cabinet experience; GX can preserve much of the content at home but not the cabinet itself.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official home release of AX as a standalone title.

primary.why: GP Legend is a GBA F-Zero entry tied to the anime era and has no modern official port documented in the sources used here.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Game Boy Advance hardware or mGBA with a legally dumped cartridge.

entries.title: F-Zero Climax

emulation.notes: GBA emulation gives clean scaling; language remains Japanese.

primary.why: F-Zero Climax is a Japan-only GBA entry and the last traditional F-Zero before F-Zero 99, with no modern official port documented in the sources used here.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese GBA cartridge on hardware or mGBA with a legally dumped copy.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English localization or modern rerelease exists.

entries.title: F-Zero 99

primary.why: F-Zero 99 is a Switch Online-exclusive battle-royale reinterpretation of the SNES game with 99-player online racing, and Switch is its only official platform.
primary.how_to_play: Download F-Zero 99 on Nintendo Switch with an active Nintendo Switch Online membership.

all_releases.fidelity: Current online battle-royale release based on the SNES game.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official platform and current service route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online-service availability and event content can change.
